sections.html:
Geneva is the county seat and the only city in Fillmore County, in southeastern Nebraska. Exeter, Fairmont, Grafton, Milligan, Ohiowa, Shickley and Strang are villages. Residents numbered 5,551 at the 2020 census and an estimated 5,458 in 2025, a small and slowly shrinking population. Corn and soybeans drive the farm economy.

The 2020 count found 2,718 housing units, 12.2% of them vacant. With that much empty stock, a house that needs work can sit on the market for months. If you hold a vacant inherited home or an unwanted rental, the wait has to be weighed against another year of taxes and upkeep.

Many houses and farmsteads go back to the 1870s, when the railroad arrived. On older property, buyers start with the roof, wiring and foundation. Low spots on the flat loess plain can pond after heavy rain or snowmelt, so look at drainage before you list.

Both real estate and personal property bills in Fillmore County are late after two dates, May 1 and September 1 (Nebraska statutes 77-203 and 77-204), and interest then runs at 14 percent. Tax notices are mailed around December 1.

Deadline or feeFillmore County rule
Early-year installmentLate after May 1
Late-year installmentLate after September 1
Weekend or holidayWhen April 30 or August 31 lands on one, the following business day is the final interest-free day
Mailed paymentsJudged by postmark
Card payments2.35 percent convenience fee

Paid receipts are no longer mailed automatically, so tuck a stamped, self-addressed envelope into your payment if you want one back. Amounts and status show on the Nebraska Taxes Online website, or you can phone the treasurer. If a notice never arrives, call the office anyway, since a missing notice doesn't move the due date. Moving? Phone the office or send the county's change of address form.

A house that sells early in the year may still owe the first half of the prior year's bill until May 1. Have the closing agent show which half is being paid and who is paying it.

The thing you can contest is the valuation, never the tax bill. Nebraska Form 422, from the Department of Revenue, goes to the county clerk, whose staff run the County Board of Equalization. For real property the deadline is June 30.

A valid protest names the value you want and gives the reason. A losing party can go on to the state's Tax Equalization and Review Commission, but only within 30 days of the board's adjournment. For the June 1 to July 25 session, July 25 is deemed the adjournment date.

Convincing proof might be a recent sale of a comparable house nearby, a repair estimate that explains a lower condition, or proof that comparable properties carry lower values. When there's a failing roof, a cracked foundation or other major defect, photos and contractor bids outweigh opinion.

Rural acreage may be taxed as agricultural land, a different valuation track from a town lot.

If tax goes unpaid, the parcel can be sold as a lien at the treasurer's yearly auction. It takes place at the courthouse at 9:00 a.m. on the first Monday in March, and for three consecutive weeks in February the local paper and Nebraska Taxes Online carry the delinquent list.

A bidder buys a lien on the parcel, not the house. Owners have three years to redeem, the certificate earns 14 percent, and the buyer must keep paying later years' delinquent taxes to hold the certificate. Should three years pass without redemption, the holder then has six months to begin foreclosure.

February is therefore a real deadline. Closing before the list runs keeps your parcel out of print, and advertising costs get added to what a certificate buyer pays. County staff can't offer legal advice, so take certificate and redemption questions to a Nebraska attorney.

Selling means paying the state's documentary stamp tax. From July 18, 2026 it's $3.32 on each $1,000 of value, rounding any fraction up to a full $1,000, and the seller as grantor is responsible. The deed must also carry a finished Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, or the register of deeds will send it back.

A few transfers are exempt, certain deeds to trustees among them. Both documents are normally drawn up by a title company or closing attorney, and the amount appears on your estimated settlement statement.

sections.h2: Roads, towns and who buys here
sections.html:
US 81 comes in from Thayer County and heads north into York County. US 6 crosses the north, Nebraska Highway 41 runs up the middle and Highway 74 follows the south. BNSF Railway tracks pass Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton.

  • Houses along US 6 and the tracks in Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton draw a different pool of buyers than farmsteads on county gravel.
  • Geneva has the courthouse, county offices and schools, which makes it the center of local interest.
  • In a county this small, a listing may bring few showings in a month, so some owners ask for a cash offer instead.

A Fillmore County sale moves through a few hands. Early on, the closing agent asks the treasurer which half-year is open and how much interest has built up. The deed and Form 521 are drafted, and the stamp tax is listed on the settlement statement. When the sale closes, any delinquent balance is taken out of your proceeds and the deed is filed with the register of deeds.

If the house is on the tax sale list and a certificate has already been sold, ask the agent for the redemption figure, because it includes the buyer's interest. Questions about a tax lien or foreclosure deadline belong with a Nebraska attorney, not the county office.

sections.h2: Selling a Fillmore County house on a deadline
sections.html:
Inherited, behind on taxes or just worn out, the house can still sell. A few steps keep it moving:

  • Ask the treasurer or closing agent for the exact payoff and which half-year is open.
  • Choose between a June 30 protest or selling and leaving the next valuation to the buyer.
  • If the parcel is headed for the February advertising list, aim to close before it runs.
  • Have the title company prepare the deed and Form 521.

Cash Home Buyers can look at a Fillmore County house and explain how an as-is offer works. The title company pays the treasurer out of your proceeds, and nobody has to tour the house, get a loan approved or negotiate repairs.

faqs.q: When are Fillmore County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After May 1 and after September 1, when 14 percent interest starts. If April 30 or August 31 is a weekend or holiday, the following business day is still interest-free.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property valuation protest in Fillmore County?
faqs.a: Nebraska Form 422 goes to the county clerk, who handles the County Board of Equalization. Real property protests are due June 30 and must give the value you want and your reason.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fillmore County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A payoff request goes from the closing agent to the treasurer, and the balance is deducted from what you receive. Closing before the February advertising run keeps your parcel off the public list.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Fillmore County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, as grantor, unless an exemption fits. The charge is $3.32 on every $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

faqs.q: How can I check what I owe the Fillmore County treasurer?
faqs.a: Look up amounts and payment status on Nebraska Taxes Online, or call the treasurer's office through the county website.
